extra_misconceptions.fact: Main branch repairs require shutting off the house main valve and opening the lowest faucet to drain residual line pressure.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Closing a fixture stop valve is sufficient preparation before repairing a main branch valve upstream of that fixture.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Capping or plugging a relief valve removes overpressure protection and can cause the water heater tank to rupture violently.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Water heater temperature and pressure relief valves can be plugged temporarily if they begin dripping onto the floor.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sewer gas contains methane, hydrogen sulfide, and airborne pathogens that create both explosion hazards and toxic exposure risks.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Sewer gas entering a bathroom through a dry floor drain is merely an unpleasant odor with no safety or health risks.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Molten solder and boiling flux frequently drip or splatter downward during overhead work, requiring full eye and hand protection.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Safety glasses are unnecessary when soldering overhead copper joints as long as the torch flame is pointed away from you.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to potable supply lines if a submerged hose experiences a sudden drop in main pressure?
Which physical clearance between a faucet spout and sink flood rim prevents back-siphonage without mechanical valves?
What temperature range on a home water heater balances scald prevention against Legionella bacterial growth?
Why is it dangerous to cut metallic water pipes before checking if they serve as the home electrical ground path?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Vent stacks equalize air pressure inside the drainage system so flowing wastewater does not siphon water seals out of fixture traps.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Plumbing vent stacks exist primarily to let foul odors escape from the household bathroom into the outdoor atmosphere.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Excessive drain slope causes liquids to flow away too rapidly, leaving solid waste stranded inside the pipe to form blockages.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Steeper horizontal drainpipe slopes always clear solid waste more reliably than a shallow quarter-inch-per-foot grade.

extra_misconceptions.fact: An attached hose traps water inside the sillcock barrel, causing it to freeze, expand, and split the copper housing inside the wall.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Leaving an outdoor garden hose attached to a frost-free sillcock during winter will not affect the indoor valve stem.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Heated water loses dissolved gases and can cool and crystallize rapidly in uninsulated exterior walls once circulation stops.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hot water lines freeze less readily than cold water lines because the water starts at a higher initial temperature.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should you open drain valves after shutting off the main supply to clear water from pipes in an unheated cabin?
Under what condition does a discharging toilet siphon the water seal out of an adjacent sink trap on the same branch line?
What downward slope per foot allows horizontal drainpipes to transport solids without liquids outrunning the waste?
Why is it dangerous to thaw a frozen water supply pipe inside a wall cavity using an open propane torch flame?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Hardened pipe wrench teeth gouge soft brass and chrome plating; use a strap wrench or smooth-jaw pliers on finished fixtures.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Serrated steel pipe wrenches are appropriate for tightening polished chrome drain traps and decorative supply nuts.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Two wrenches must be used in opposing directions so one backs up the stationary pipe and prevents twisting joints inside the wall.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A single pipe wrench is sufficient when unscrewing a corroded galvanized coupling from an older threaded standpipe.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Wheel cutters roll a sharp metal ridge inward that causes flow turbulence and erosion unless removed with a reaming tool.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cutting copper tubing with a wheel cutter leaves a clean interior edge that is ready for immediate fluxing and soldering.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cup plungers seal on flat sink and tub surfaces, whereas toilet bowls require an extended soft rubber flange to seal the horn.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Flange plungers and flat-bottom cup plungers work interchangeably on both flat sink drains and contoured toilet bowls.

extra_socratic_questions: Which direction must the open jaws of an adjustable pipe wrench face relative to your pull so the teeth bite into the pipe?
What design feature enables a basin wrench to tighten faucet mounting nuts recessed deep behind a narrow sink bowl?
What happens to the copper wall thickness if you tighten a tubing cutter feed screw too aggressively on a single rotation?
Why is it dangerous to slip a cheater pipe extension over a pipe wrench handle when breaking loose a rusted steel fitting?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Flux dissolves surface oxides and promotes capillary action so molten metal solder can bond directly to the bare copper walls.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rosin flux prevents leaks by acting as an adhesive sealant that glues copper tubing directly inside a sweat fitting.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A plug has external male threads that screw inside a fitting, whereas a cap has internal female threads that screw over a pipe end.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A threaded pipe plug and a pipe cap have identical threads and can be swapped freely when sealing the end of a pipe.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Unthreading one end of a rigid pipe tightens the opposite end; a three-piece union is required to disconnect mid-run piping.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A standard threaded coupling allows a middle section of galvanized steel pipe to be unthreaded without cutting the line.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A trap holds a standing water seal that blocks toxic sewer gases and vermin from rising through the drainpipe into living spaces.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The primary purpose of a sink P-trap is to catch dropped jewelry and heavy debris before those items enter the sewer main.

extra_socratic_questions: Where in a rigid threaded steel pipeline would you install a union instead of a standard coupling to allow future servicing?
What chemical action does paste flux perform on heated copper surfaces so molten lead-free solder flows into the joint gap?
Which indicator on a residential water meter dial confirms a hidden supply leak when every fixture inside the house is shut off?
Why is it dangerous to use fifty-fifty tin-lead acid-core solder when sweating copper fittings on a kitchen drinking water line?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Standard PVC softens and degrades above 140 degrees Fahrenheit; hot water supply lines require CPVC, PEX, or copper piping.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: White Schedule 40 PVC pipe is rated for indoor hot water supply lines running directly from a residential water heater.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Type K has the thickest wall for underground burial, Type L is medium weight for interiors, and Type M is the thinnest wall grade.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Type M thin-wall copper tubing is the heaviest grade of copper pipe and is preferred for buried underground water services.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Dense cast iron dampens the sound of rushing water far better than plastic and does not emit toxic fumes during a building fire.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cast iron soil pipe is obsolete in modern buildings because plastic PVC drainpipe conducts less noise between floors.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cross-linked polyethylene does not dissolve in solvent cement and must be joined with crimp rings, expansion rings, or push fittings.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: PEX tubing can be solvent-welded directly into PVC fittings using standard purple primer and clear plastic pipe cement.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to cross-linked polyethylene tubing if it is installed outdoors where it receives direct daily sunlight exposure?
Which material property allows CPVC pipe to carry domestic hot water safely while standard PVC is limited to cold lines?
What color-coded stripe identifies thick-walled Type K copper tubing approved for underground trench service lines?
Why is it dangerous to install uncoated black steel pipe on a potable drinking water line instead of fuel gas piping?

extra_misconceptions.fact: The torch must heat the fitting cup opposite the solder so capillary action draws molten metal cleanly into the entire joint.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Applying torch heat directly to the tip of the solder wire is the fastest way to fill a copper sweat fitting completely.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Compression fittings seal where the brass ferrule wedges against the tube and valve seat; tape on the nut threads hinders tightening.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wrapping PTFE thread tape over the threads of a brass compression nut stops leaks at the ferrule of a supply stop valve.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Primer chemically softens and penetrates the rigid PVC surface so the solvent cement can fuse the pipe and socket into one piece.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Purple primer on PVC pipe is merely an optional cleaner that removes dirt before the glue adheres the two surfaces together.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sudden quenching causes thermal shock that cracks the cooling solder; let the joint cool naturally before wiping away flux residue.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cooling a freshly soldered copper joint immediately with a wet rag strengthens the metal bond and speeds up pressure testing.

extra_socratic_questions: Why must you give a PVC pipe a quarter-turn as you push it into a cemented socket and hold it firmly for fifteen seconds?
Which direction must PTFE thread seal tape be wrapped around male pipe threads so screwing on the fitting does not unravel it?
What measurement tool verifies that a copper crimp ring has been compressed to the exact diameter required on a PEX barb fitting?
Where should a flame-resistant heat shield and fire extinguisher be staged before sweating a copper joint near wood wall studs?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most jurisdictions require passing a master plumber examination and carrying contractor insurance before pulling permits independently.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A journeyman plumber license automatically grants legal authority to pull municipal permits and operate an independent business.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Registered plumbing apprenticeships use an earn-while-you-learn model where apprentices receive wages during on-the-job training.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Trade apprentices must pay full tuition upfront before they are allowed to begin working alongside licensed journeymen on job sites.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Pipefitters specialize in high-pressure industrial piping for steam, chemicals, and power generation rather than residential fixtures.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pipefitters and residential plumbers install identical low-pressure domestic water and sanitary drainage fixtures in houses.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Plumbers must complete continuing education for updated building codes and hold specialized certifications for medical gas or backflow.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Once a master plumber earns state licensure, no further code classes or specialty endorsements are needed throughout a career.

extra_socratic_questions: What combination of supervised on-the-job hours and classroom instruction is required to advance from apprentice to journeyman?
Which technical systems distinguish the daily work of an industrial steamfitter from that of a residential service plumber?
What information must a municipal plumbing inspector verify and sign off on before rough-in pipes are concealed behind drywall?
Why is it dangerous for a utility pipe layer to enter an unshored trench deeper than five feet to connect a municipal sewer main?
